entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Lazaros of Mount Galesios was an 11th-century Byzantine monk and stylite who founded a monastic community at Mount Galesios near Ephesus.

Born into a noble family in the late 10th century, Lazaros studied theology and philosophy in Constantinople, where he became known for his asceticism and mystical experiences.

In 1045, Lazaros renounced his worldly life and began a 40-year sojourn on Mount Galesios, where he built a small chapel and lived a simple, ascetic life, devoting himself to prayer and contemplation.

Lazaros's community attracted pilgrims from across the Byzantine Empire, and his reputation as a holy man spread far and wide.

Despite his isolation, Lazaros maintained a connection to the outside world, responding to letters from his supporters and engaging in correspondence with prominent theologians of his time.

Lazaros of Mount Galesios died on November 8, 1054, and was buried in the chapel he had built on Mount Galesios, where his relics were later venerated by pilgrims.

This legacy has endured for centuries, with Lazaros remaining a revered figure in Byzantine hagiography and a symbol of spiritual devotion in the Orthodox Church.
